title: Add users
t1: In Adobe Admin Console, open the Experience Platform product and add the user's email to the AEP Default All Users product profile.
t2: In the Platform UI under Permissions > Roles, create a role and choose its sandboxes and feature permissions.
t3: Open the role's Users tab, select Add Users, and add the user to grant the configured access.

title: Add developers
t1: In Adobe Admin Console, open Experience Platform's product profile, go to the Developers tab, and add the developer's email.
t2: After the developer generates API credentials in Developer Console, go to Permissions > Roles, open a role's API Credentials tab, and add their credentials.
t3: On the same role's Users tab, add the developer as a user so they can test their integrations in the Platform UI.

title: Configure attribute-based access control
t1: Open the role's Labels tab and add the data-usage label (for example, Regulated Health Data) to the role.
t2: Open the schema (and audience) and add the same label to the fields and objects you want to restrict.
t3: Go to Permissions > Policies and activate the Default Label-Based Access Control policy to enforce the restriction.

title: Create and populate a dataset
t1: Select Datasets in the left nav, click Create Dataset, choose Create Dataset from schema, pick the schema, name it, and click Finish.
t2: In the Add Data panel, drag the data file into the dataset to start a batch and wait for the batch status to reach Success.
t3: Toggle the Profile button on in the right panel and confirm to enable the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile.

title: Create destinations and activate data
t1: In Destinations > Catalog, find the desired destination.
t2: On the destination card, select Set up (or configure a new instance).
t3: Enter the required credentials and select Connect to destination to authenticate and verify the connection.

title: Create merge policies
t1: Select Profiles > Merge Policies, click Create Merge Policy, then name it and set its class, ID stitching, and default options; select Next.
t2: Choose the merge method (Timestamp ordered or Dataset precedence) and select Next.
t3: Review the merge policy details and select Finish to save it.

title: Create schemas
t1: Select Schemas in the left nav, click Create Schema, and choose a base class (for example, Individual Profile); select Next.
t2: Give the schema a name and optional description, then click Finish.
t3: Add fields by typing field names or adding field groups (for example, the Loyalty field group) to the schema.

title: Use sandboxes (reset a development sandbox)
t1: Go to Sandboxes in the left nav and select the development sandbox you want to reset.
t2: Select Sandbox Reset and acknowledge the warning that all user-created resources will be deleted.
t3: Manually type the sandbox name to confirm and select Reset to return it to a clean state.

title: Copy packages between sandboxes
t1: In the source (development) sandbox, create a package and add the objects (schemas, journeys, and so on) to it.
t2: On the package inventory page, review the artifacts and Publish the package.
t3: From the target sandbox, select Import, choose the target sandbox, review dependencies, and import the package.

title: Share packages across IMS Orgs
t1: In the source org, open Partner Orgs > Manage Partner Orgs, enter the target org ID, and submit a sharing request.
t2: An admin in the target org reviews and approves the incoming partnership request.
t3: Back in the source org's package inventory, select the package, choose the approved org, and submit the share job.
